r0040: The president, one full member, one substitute member and the public prosecutor shall be chosen, in accordance with procedures laid down in special legislation, from among judges and public prosecutors of the Republic of the first rank, one full member and one substitute member from among military judges of the first rank, and the assistant prosecutors from among public prosecutors of the Republic and military judges.
r0041: The presidents and the full and substitute members ... of national security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) shall be appointed for a renewable term of four years.
r0042: The Court of Cassation (*Cour de cassation*) shall hear appeals against judgments of national security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) ...”
r0043: 21.  Law no. 4388 of 18 June 1999 on the establishment of national security courts (*loi relative à l’instauration des cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) amended Article 143 of the Constitution, which now reads as follows:
r0044: “... National security courts (*cours de sûreté de l’Etat*) shall consist of a president, two full members, one substitute member, a chief public prosecutor of the Republic and a sufficient number of public prosecutors of the Republic.
r0045: The president, two full members, one substitute member and the chief public prosecutor of the Republic shall be appointed from among judges and public prosecutors of the first rank, and the public prosecutors of the Republic from among public prosecutors of other ranks, for a term of four years, by the Supreme Council of Judges and Public Prosecutors, in accordance with the procedure laid down in special legislation. Their term of office shall be renewable ...”
r0047: I.  ALLEGED VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 6 OF THE CONVENTION
r0048: 22.  The applicant alleged that the National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) which had tried and convicted him was not an “independent and impartial tribunal” capable of guaranteeing him a fair trial, on account of, firstly, the presence of a military judge on its bench and, secondly, the absence of a lawyer during his police custody. He submitted that there had been a violation of Article 6 §§ 1 and 3 (c) of the Convention, the relevant parts of which provide:
r0049: “In the determination of ... any criminal charge against him, everyone is entitled to a fair and public hearing ... by an independent and impartial tribunal ...”.
